channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [8] Electron orbitals choose a direction
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Pochang Chen, Md Shafayat Hossain

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Orbital order study using electronic band structure relevant to ARPES/condensed matter physics.

Tags: #band-structure #orbital-order #intermetallics

Abstract: Orbital order is difficult to isolate because it often intertwines with lattice and magnetic transitions. Now, a study on an intermetallic compound reveals a surface 5d-orbital order through its electronic band structure and real-space fingerprints.

item.title: [9] Observation of superconductivity-induced leading-edge gap in a bilayer nickelate
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Donglai Feng, Yuefeng Nie

Authors: Wenjie Sun, Zhicheng Jiang, Bo Hao, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Donglai Feng

Tags: #nickelate #superconduct #Fermisurface

Abstract: Superconductivity has been demonstrated in La3Ni2O7, and now the structure of the superconducting gap is observed. The Fermi surface is shown to derive mainly from the $${d}_{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$$ d x 2 − y 2 bands, with minimal involvement from the $${d}_{{z}^{2}}$$ d z 2 band.

item.title: [6] Electrons do more than just flow
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Broad perspective on electronic degrees of freedom in quantum materials.

Tags: #quantum-materials #electronic-degrees-of-freedom

Abstract: Recent advances in quantum materials have shifted the focus from charge transport to a broader range of electronic degrees of freedom. In this Focus issue, we highlight different facets of electronic degrees of freedom and their potential applications.
